source: TH Software Tuition 2026 SE Trial (papers/2026 TH Software Tuition SE Trial.pdf) Section II Q1
prompt:
Trace through the SQL query below and explain exactly what it returns, describing the effect of each clause in order.

```sql
SELECT category_id, COUNT(*)
FROM posts
WHERE published = 1
GROUP BY category_id;
```
sample_answer: FROM posts selects the table; WHERE published = 1 keeps only published rows; GROUP BY category_id groups the remaining rows by category; SELECT returns one row per category_id with COUNT(*), the number of published posts in that category.

source: TH Software Tuition 2026 SE Trial (papers/2026 TH Software Tuition SE Trial.pdf) Section II Q2
prompt:
The query below is intended to join every post to its author’s username, but it contains a syntax error. Identify the error and rewrite the query correctly.

```sql
SELECT users.username, posts.title
FROM users
INNER JOIN posts WHERE users.id = posts.author_id;
```
sample_answer: The INNER JOIN has no ON clause (WHERE cannot supply the join condition). Corrected: SELECT users.username, posts.title FROM users INNER JOIN posts ON users.id = posts.author_id;
